description:
Date-driven terms show the day of the month by which payment is due and can include a discount for early payment. For example, the following date-driven term means that payment is due on the 30th of the month, with a 1% discount if payment is made by the 10th:

The `date_driven_terms_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted. Returns the v2 request to send, and the webhook payload QuickBooks' answer arrives in (this operation's response_json: its data shape and the status codes to handle).

Possible errors (error.code / error.type; the call result explains each): 1030 unsupported_request, 3040 invalid_amount, 3070 string_too_long, 3100 name_in_use, 3150 missing_element, 3175 in_use, 3176 locked, 3180 cannot_save, 3210 invalid_value, 3220 not_authorized, 3231 request_not_processed, 3250 feature_not_enabled, 3260 insufficient_permission, 3261 personal_data_access_denied, 3262 payroll_subscription_required, 3263 read_only_access, 3264 merchant_services_subscription_required, 3270 missing_posting_account

day_of_month_due.description: The day of the month when full payment is due with no discount.

discount_day_of_month.description: If the payment is made by this day of the month, then `discount_pct` applies.

discount_pct.description: If payment is received by `discount_day_of_month`, then this discount will apply to the payment. `discount_pct` must be between 0 and 100.

due_next_month_days.description: Handles cases when an invoice or bill is issued close to its due date. If the invoice or bill is issued within this many days of the due date, payment isn’t due until the following month.

include_qbxml.description: Also return the qbXML this compiles to, for debugging. Not part of the v2 request.

is_active.description: If `is_active` is true, this object is currently enabled for use by QuickBooks. The default value is true.

name.description: Name is the case-insensitive short name of a list object (without ancestors). It must be unique within its hierarchy scope.

request_id.description: Your own label for the request, sent to QuickBooks as its qbXML `requestID` and echoed in the raw answer (`response_xml`); optional, since the answer's webhook already carries the request's `id`.

body.description: The JSON body: the arguments you passed.

headers.description: Send with the request. Resent unchanged when no 201 came back, it answers with the request already queued.

qbxml.description: The qbXML it compiles to. Only with include_qbxml.

webhook.description: JSON Schema of the payload POSTed to webhook_url once QuickBooks answers, with this operation's response_json (data shape and status codes).
